A separate colony logic mod: live sensors, editable rules and a ladder window.

RimPLC

RimPLC is a separate mod for colony rules. It reads the colony, evaluates your conditions and shows the matching advice in an in-game ladder window. Rimrooms does not require it, and RimPLC does not require Rimrooms, another mod or an expansion. It uses no Harmony.

Game versions

RimPLC is being prepared for RimWorld 1.7 unstable / Waylith, with 1.6 retained. Both game versions load the same 1.7/ content folder. The inspected compiler and API baseline is 1.6; 1.7 runtime compatibility has not been verified.

The official announcement explains the engine update and unstable branch. A version declaration does not replace an actual result on that version.

What you can do

ViewPurpose
LadderSee which rules are true, false, unmeasured or unresolved; enable, edit or add a rule
TagsSet bounded thresholds used by rules
MarksKeep a named boolean or number for a judgement the game cannot measure
SensorsInspect the values read from the colony
LogReview notices and recorded outputs

Sensors include health, mood, food, materials, threats, research, temperature, alerts and buildings. A missing value stays unmeasured; it does not become a guessed zero. Definitions are looked up by name, so a rule whose required mod or expansion is absent stays unavailable.

Rules support comparisons, OR, NOT, timers, counters and one-shot conditions. Their memory is saved with the colony, and timers advance in game ticks.

Advice and automatic outputs

Advice is the default. A matching rule can tell you what to do next. In the current implementation, automatic outputs are limited to messages, marks and tags.

RimPLC does not currently carry out world-changing actions such as drafting pawns, placing blueprints, building a gate or changing work priorities. A plan describing those actions is not an implemented output. Keep the game's normal controls available.

Presets and saved rules

The supplied ladder is a preset. Editing one of its rules creates a player override; reverting returns to the preset. Player rules, switches, marks, tag overrides and instruction memory are stored in the save.

Export and import use the game's configuration folder under RimPLC/exports/. An import shows its changes before you apply it. Back up a colony before changing its rules or switching game versions; save and load behavior on 1.7 remains unverified.

Optional bridge access

The core mod needs no bridge. Its optional companion exposes rule reads and edits through RimBridgeServer. The companion DLL belongs in the game's BridgeTools/RimPLC/ folder, separate from the mod package, and requires a matching installed bridge SDK.

Without that bridge, supported commands use RimPLC/inbox.jsonl and outbox.jsonl in the game's configuration folder. The in-game window remains available either way. Owner-only changes stay restricted to the owner route.

Getting it

RimPLC on Forgejo and RimPLC on GitHub are the project repositories. Use its documented package or build instructions; the source checkout is not a finished Workshop installation. Place the loadable package in RimWorld's Local Mods folder with About/ directly inside it. Leave the shared 1.7/ folder name unchanged.

RimPLC and Rimrooms are independently enabled mods. A Rimrooms sensor link is separate integration work; installing both does not prove that link exists or that 1.7 compatibility has passed.

For Rimrooms installation, see Install. For the project addresses, see Links.
